review_method.checkout: The pinned cobra checkout in the session scratchpad was confirmed at a0a6ae020bb3899ff0276067863e50523f897370 with a clean working tree before any span was read.
review_method.span_check: Every judgement was checked mechanically and then by eye: file exists, 1 <= start_line <= end_line <= number of lines in the file, and the anchor string occurs literally within the cited lines. All 30 judgements of the 7 candidates passed; no span was out of range and no anchor was missing.
review_method.boundary_check: Each span was read together with the lines above and below it to test the draft's own span_convention (start at the first line of the doc comment, end at the closing brace in column 0). One violation was found and corrected (cq-05 judgement 3).
review_method.reason_check: Reasons were treated as claims. Checkable factual claims were verified against the checkout - call graphs by grep over the pinned tree. Two were wrong or imprecise and were rewritten (cq-07 judgement 3, cq-02 judgement 1). Interpretive shorthand that points a reader at the right thing was left alone and is named in the verdict notes.
review_method.collision_check: Every span was compared against internal/eval/retrieval/testdata/datasets/cobra-v2.json and docs/eval/retrieval/drafts/2026-09-14-holdout-shaped-dev/dataset.json, and every query string against both files' query texts. This is where cq-02's duplicate of cd-70 surfaced; the draft's collision table had only compared spans against cobra-v2.json.
not_checked: Candidates outside stratum exact_identifier - another reviewer's lot.
family_id derivation and uniqueness: taken from the draft, not recomputed.

queries.r1_review_note: Rejected as a duplicate, not as bad evidence. All four spans were read at the pinned checkout and are correct. But docs/eval/retrieval/drafts/2026-09-14-holdout-shaped-dev/dataset.json (id cobra-v3-dev-reviewed, declared usable as a development split, already independently reviewed) carries cd-70: the same query string 'GenBashCompletionV2', the same stratum exact_identifier, the same split dev, and the byte-identical grade-3 span bash_completionsV2.go:392-396 - under a different family_id (cobra-family-83b084be11bacec7 vs this candidate's cobra-family-8c733ade6fba3574). Two identical queries in two families defeats exactly what family_id exists for, and would leak across the split the moment one family is assigned to holdout. The draft's own collision table missed this because it compared spans against cobra-v2.json only, while checking family ids repository-wide. Releasing this needs an owner decision (merge into cd-70's family, or drop one row), not a reviewer sign-off.

verdicts.note: MarkFlagsOneRequired. All four spans read at the pinned checkout and correct: flag_groups.go:47-61 is the declaration with its doc comment, :167-186 is validateOneRequiredFlagGroups (no doc comment above it, so the span rightly starts at the func line), :25-29 is the annotation-key const block that MarkFlagsOneRequired writes through SetAnnotation, and flag_groups_test.go:22-195 is the whole table test, which does exercise one-required groups (cases at lines 68-71, 83-86, 98-101, 114-118, 140-147). The draft's own review_note flags that the test span is also cb-02's grade-1 span; I keep it, because cobra-v2.json reuses spans across families as a matter of course. Grade 2 for the const block matches cobra-v2.json's cb-26, which grades the analogous active_help.go const block a 2.

GenBashCompletionV2. Not released: verbatim duplicate of cd-70 in docs/eval/retrieval/drafts/2026-09-14-holdout-shaped-dev/dataset.json - same query, same stratum, same split, same grade-3 span bash_completionsV2.go:392-396, different family_id. See r1_review_note on the query. The spans themselves are sound (392-396, 24-29, 381-390 all end at a column-0 closing brace; the doc section site/content/completions/_index.md:421-451 runs exactly to the next heading at :452), and judgement 1's reason was corrected for precision, but the duplicate is an owner decision, not something a reviewer may wave through.

AppendActiveHelp. active_help.go:35-44 is the declaration with its seven-line doc comment; :24-31 is the const block holding activeHelpMarker, which the function prefixes; :46-57 is GetActiveHelpConfig; completions.go:216-221 is a coherent sub-span (the whole 'if ActiveHelp disabled' branch inside the hidden __complete command's Run) and is where marked entries are dropped; site/content/active_help.md:24-29 is exactly the '## Adding Active Help messages' section, ending before the next heading at :30, and line 28 names cobra.AppendActiveHelp. I let judgement 2's reason stand although 'decides whether the appended messages survive' is loose - GetActiveHelpConfig reports the configured value and completions.go:216 makes the decision. That is an interpretive shorthand, not a false fact, so it does not meet my amendment bar.

FixedCompletions. Declaration (completions.go:124-130), sibling NoFileCompletions (:118-122) and the ShellCompDirective const block (:54-94, opening 'const (' to closing ')') all check out. Amended judgement 2: completions.go:502-517 was graded 2 and is downgraded to 1 - the span is the generic completion dispatch, contains no mention of FixedCompletions, and would be equally returned for any completion query. Keeping it at 2 while cq-07 grades a span that literally calls its queried symbol a 1 would make the grade scale incoherent.

GenYamlCustom. doc/yaml_docs.go:92-147 (declaration), :87-90 (GenYaml, which really does pass an identity link handler) and :149-175 (genFlagResult, really called at :113 and :117 to fill the cmdDoc) are correct. Amended judgement 3: the span was 30-51 and ran past both struct bodies - cmdOption closes at :35, cmdDoc at :46 - into lines 48-51, the first four lines of GenYamlTree's doc comment, cut mid-sentence. Corrected to 30-46, which is precisely the two document structs the reason claims. The draft's own review_note about cd-08 (GenYamlTreeCustom) is resolved: different symbol, different span (doc/yaml_docs.go:59-85), different family_id, no duplicate.

MatchAll. args.go:113-123 is the declaration; :125-131 is the deprecated ExactValidArgs, whose body is literally MatchAll(ExactArgs(n), OnlyValidArgs); args.go:22-22 is the PositionalArgs type MatchAll takes and returns - a one-line span, which I checked against precedent before accepting: cobra-v2.json's ci-827 uses the identical single-line span at grade 2. args_test.go:440-486 is TestMatchAll; site/content/user_guide.md:367-421 is exactly the '## Positional and Custom Arguments' section, ending before '## Example' at :422, and line 384 documents MatchAll explicitly. Grade 1 for that doc section is conservative - it explains MatchAll by name and with an example, so a 2 would be defensible - but under-grading does not corrupt the authorisation, so I leave it.

LocalNonPersistentFlags. command.go:1655-1666 (declaration), :1668-1693 (LocalFlags, which it iterates) and :1725-1735 (PersistentFlags, whose members it filters out) are correct. Amended judgement 3: the reason claimed completions.go:437-448 is the symbol's 'only in-tree caller'. That is false - bash_completions.go:565 calls it too, in the V1 bash script generator, for the same purpose. Reason corrected; the span, the grade and the functional claim about subcommand completion (confirmed at completions.go:450-454) stand.
